concepts.name: Wages follow work done
concepts.description: When workers are paid at the same rate, money is split in the ratio of work done.

concepts.name: Wages from days taken
concepts.description: Faster workers take fewer days, so their share is proportional to 1 ÷ days.

concepts.name: Man-days and daily rates
concepts.description: Total pay is workers × days × daily rate; hours work the same way.

concepts.name: Changing crews
concepts.description: Work out each person's fraction of the whole job, then split the money by those fractions.

formulas.title: Split by work done
formulas.prompt: Two workers are paid at the same rate for a job. How is the total split?
formulas.explanation: Equal pay per unit of work means total pay is proportional to units of work.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A and B did 3 : 2 of a job and earned ₹1,500. What does A get?

formulas.title: Wages from time taken
formulas.prompt: A and B finish a job alone in a and b days. If they work together, how do they split the pay?
formulas.explanation: A worker who takes fewer days does more each day. In equal time, work done is proportional to the daily rate.
formulas.commonMistake: Using the days themselves as the ratio (10 : 15 = 2 : 3).
formulas.applicationPrompt: A takes 10 days and B takes 15 days alone. In what ratio do they share the wages?

formulas.title: Total wages
formulas.prompt: N workers each earn w per day and work for d days. What is the total wage bill?
formulas.explanation: Each worker earns w every day, so multiply by workers and days.
formulas.commonMistake: Forgetting to multiply by the number of days.
formulas.applicationPrompt: How much do 8 workers earn in 12 days at ₹150 per day each?

formulas.title: Changing crews
formulas.prompt: Workers join or leave part-way through. How is pay divided?
formulas.formula:
Share of A = (A's fraction of the whole job) ÷ 1
Fraction = rate × days worked
formulas.explanation: Work out the fraction of the job each person completed, checking that the fractions total 1.
formulas.example: A does 1/10 per day for 5 days = 1/2
formulas.commonMistake: Paying by days worked without adjusting for different rates.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A does 1/10 per day and B does 1/15 per day. Both work 5 days and C finishes the rest. What fraction did C complete?

formulas.title: The helper's share
formulas.prompt: A and B alone take a and b days. With C they finish in t days. What is C's share of the wage?
formulas.formula: C's share = 1 − t/a − t/b of the total
formulas.explanation: In t days A does t/a of the job and B does t/b; C did the rest and is paid for it.
formulas.example: A 6 days, B 8 days, with C 3 days, wage ₹3,200: C does 1 − 1/2 − 3/8 = 1/8, so ₹400.
formulas.commonMistake: Splitting the wage equally among the three.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A and B take 10 and 15 days; with C they take 5 days. Out of ₹1,500, what does C get?

levels.title: Pay Follows Work
levels.description: Turn time-and-work rates into a fair split of the money.

blocks.title: Same rate per unit of work
blocks.body: If everyone is paid the same per unit of work, the total money is split in the ratio of work done. So the whole problem becomes: what fraction of the job did each person do?

blocks.title: Working from days
blocks.body: Alone in a and b days → A : B = 1/a : 1/b
blocks.caption: The quicker worker does more each day, so gets a larger share.

blocks.body: A common trap: sharing in the ratio of days taken. That rewards the slower worker. Always convert days into rates first.

levels.title: Wages Formulas
levels.description: Work splits, rates from days, total wage bills and changing crews.

levels.title: Rates, Efficiency and Man-Days
levels.description: Split the pay by rates and man-days.

levels.title: Crews That Change
levels.description: Third workers, leaving workers and hour totals.

questions.question: A does 1/3 of a piece of work and B does the remaining 2/3. They are paid ₹900 in total. How much does B get?
questions.explanation: B did 2/3 of the work, so B gets 2/3 of ₹900 = ₹600.
questions.method: Split the money in the ratio of work done.

hints.text: Who did more of the work?

questions.question: A and B do work in the ratio 3 : 2 and are paid ₹1,500 in total. How much does A get, in rupees?
questions.explanation: Total parts = 5, so one part = ₹300. A gets 3 parts = ₹900.
questions.method: Divide the total by the sum of the ratio terms.

hints.text: Add the ratio terms to find the total number of parts.

questions.question: A can finish a job in 10 days and B in 15 days. They work together and share the wages. In what ratio should A and B share?
questions.explanation: Daily rates: A = 1/10, B = 1/15, which is 3/30 : 2/30 = 3 : 2. The quicker worker does more and earns more.

hints.text: Convert each time into a daily rate.

commonMistakes: Using the days directly (10 : 15 = 2 : 3), which pays the slower worker more.

questions.question: When two workers finish a job together at the same pay rate, their wages are divided in proportion to

options.text: the number of days each would take alone

questions.explanation: Wages track work done. The days each would take alone give the reverse ratio, so they cannot be used directly.

hints.text: A worker who takes longer alone does less per day.

questions.question: 5 workers each work 6 days at ₹200 per day. What is the total wage bill, in rupees?
A alone can do a job in 12 days and B alone in 24 days. They complete it together and earn ₹1,800. How much does A get, in rupees?

hints.text: Convert the times into rates and compare.

questions.question: A, B and C can finish a job alone in 6, 8 and 12 days. They work together and earn ₹1,800. How much does C get?
questions.method: Convert days into rates using the LCM.

hints.text: Take the LCM as the size of the job in units.
How many units per day does each do?

commonMistakes: Using the days themselves as the ratio (6 : 8 : 12).

questions.question: A can do a job alone in 15 days and B in 10 days. They complete it together for ₹4,200. How much does B get, in rupees?
questions.explanation: Rates 1/15 : 1/10 = 2 : 3. B does 3/5 of the work and gets 3/5 of ₹4,200 = ₹2,520.

questions.question: 12 men finish a job in 20 days for a total wage bill of ₹48,000. What is the daily wage of one man?

hints.text: How many man-days were worked altogether?

commonMistakes: Dividing by 12 only (₹4,000 is a man's wage for the whole job).

questions.question: A is twice as efficient as B. They work for the same time and are paid ₹2,700 in total. How much does A get, in rupees?
questions.explanation: Efficiency 2 : 1, and equal time means work done 2 : 1. A gets 2/3 of ₹2,700 = ₹1,800.

hints.text: Equal times means the ratio of work equals the ratio of efficiencies.

questions.question: A alone can do a job in 10 days and B alone in 15 days. With C's help they finish it in 5 days. The total payment is ₹3,600. How much does C get, in rupees?
questions.explanation: In 5 days A does 5/10 = 1/2 and B does 5/15 = 1/3. C does 1 − 1/2 − 1/3 = 1/6. C's share is 1/6 of ₹3,600 = ₹600.
questions.method: Find what is left over for the third worker.

hints.text: How much work do A and B each do in 5 days?

questions.question: A can do a job in 24 days and B in 16 days. They work together for 6 days, then A leaves and B finishes the rest. The total payment is ₹4,800. How much does B get, in rupees?
questions.explanation: A works 6 days: 6/24 = 1/4 of the job. So B does the remaining 3/4. B gets 3/4 of ₹4,800 = ₹3,600. Check: B works 6 days (3/8) then 6 more days (3/8): 3/4 ✓.
questions.method: A's fraction is rate × days; B gets the rest.

hints.text: How much did A do in his 6 days?
B's share is everything A did not do.

commonMistakes: Splitting by rates only, ignoring that B worked longer.

questions.question: A works 8 hours a day for 5 days and B works 6 hours a day for 10 days. They are paid at the same hourly rate for a job worth ₹2,400 in total. How much does B get?
questions.explanation: A works 8 × 5 = 40 hours and B works 6 × 10 = 60 hours. Ratio 2 : 3, so B gets 3/5 of ₹2,400 = ₹1,440.
questions.method: Compare total hours, not hours per day or days.

hints.text: Work out total hours for each person.

commonMistakes: Comparing days only (5 : 10) or hours per day only (8 : 6).
